22	// The signature check of the base images a repository builds on (§3.82).
23	//
24	// A base image in use that violates its rule is worse than any candidate: it is
25	// what the next build takes. It is a finding of the Misconfiguration category,
26	// anchored on the FROM line, on the build-context check's model (§3.81): DevDesk
27	// runs it, no scanner is ticked for it. Every stage counts, a build stage too —
28	// a compromised builder writes the binary the final image ships.
29	//
30	// A finding states a fact, so only a verdict that proves something produces
31	// one: a signature by someone else, or none where a rule asks for one. A check
32	// that could not run is an error of the stage, never a finding.
33	
34	// The rule ids, in DevDesk's own namespace.
35	const (
36		SignatureMismatchID = "DEVDESK-SIG-001"
37		SignatureUnsignedID = "DEVDESK-SIG-002"
38	)
39	
40	// signatureStageTimeout bounds the stage: a few cosign runs per base image.
41	const signatureStageTimeout = 5 * time.Minute
42	
43	// SignatureDeps is the production wiring of a check: the user's policy, cosign
44	// as tool resolved it and cached, the registry through the engine's
45	// credentials. The scan and every pull use this one.
46	func SignatureDeps(tool ToolSpec) trust.CheckDeps {
47		return trust.CheckDeps{
48			Policy:   trust.LoadDefault,
49			Verifier: trust.Cached(CosignVerifier{Tool: tool, Creds: registryCreds}, trust.FileStore{}, time.Now),
50			Digest:   registryDigest,
51		}
52	}
53	
54	// signatureDeps is SignatureDeps, swapped by tests.
55	var signatureDeps = SignatureDeps
56	
57	// registryCreds hands cosign what the engine holds for a host, anonymous
58	// otherwise — the same credentials a pull uses.
59	func registryCreds(host string) (string, string) {
60		user, pass, _ := docker.GetStoredCreds(host)
61		return user, pass
62	}
63	
64	// registryDigest asks the registry what ref's tag points to now. A reference
65	// with no tag is `latest`, as the engine reads it.
66	func registryDigest(ref string) (string, error) {
67		host, repo, _ := strings.Cut(trust.Repository(ref), "/")
68		registry := host
69		if host == "docker.io" {
70			registry = ""
71		}
72		user, pass, _ := docker.GetStoredCreds(host)
73		return oci.ManifestDigest(oci.RegistryAPIBase(registry), repo, tagOf(ref), user, pass)
74	}
75	
76	// tagOf is a reference's tag, "latest" when it has none.
77	func tagOf(ref string) string {
78		s, _, _ := strings.Cut(ref, "@")
79		if i := strings.LastIndex(s, ":"); i > strings.LastIndex(s, "/") {
80			return s[i+1:]
81		}
82		return "latest"
83	}
84	
85	// checksSignatures reports whether the scan runs the check: a directory, the
86	// Misconfiguration category on, and a context that verifies images.
87	func (s *Scanner) checksSignatures(targetType TargetType) bool {
88		return s.checksBuildContext(targetType) && s.options.ImageVerification != config.ImageVerificationOff
89	}
90	
91	// runSignatureStage checks every base image of every Dockerfile under target,
92	// each reference once however many stages name it.
93	func runSignatureStage(ctx context.Context, target string, deps trust.CheckDeps, result *Result, mu *sync.Mutex, notify func(ProgressUpdate)) {
94		const stage, label = "signature", "Base image signatures"
95		notify(ProgressUpdate{Stage: stage, Label: label, Status: StageRunning})
96		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, signatureStageTimeout)
97		defer cancel()
98	
99		findings, errs := checkBaseImageSignatures(ctx, target, deps)
100		mu.Lock()
101		defer mu.Unlock()
102		result.Findings = append(result.Findings, findings...)
103		for _, err := range errs {
104			recordStageError(result, "signature", err)
105		}
106		status := StageDone
107		if len(errs) > 0 {
108			status = StageError
109		}
110		notify(ProgressUpdate{Stage: stage, Label: label, Status: status})
111	}
112	
113	func checkBaseImageSignatures(ctx context.Context, target string, deps trust.CheckDeps) ([]Finding, []error) {
114		files, _, err := dockerfile.Find(target)
115		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
116			// The scanners asked to read it say so themselves: one missing
117			// directory is one error, not one per stage — build-context's rule.
118			return nil, nil
119		}
120		if err != nil {
121			return nil, []error{err}
122		}
123		verdicts := map[string]trust.Result{}
124		reported := map[string]bool{}
125		var findings []Finding
126		var errs []error
127		for _, rel := range files {
128			content, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(target, filepath.FromSlash(rel))) //nolint:gosec // a Dockerfile of the directory being scanned
129			if err != nil {
130				log.Printf("ERROR [scan/signature] read %s: %v", rel, err)
131				continue
132			}
133			for _, st := range dockerfile.Parse(content).Stages {
134				if st.Kind != dockerfile.KindImage || st.Image == "" {
135					continue
136				}
137				res, seen := verdicts[st.Image]
138				if !seen {
139					res, _ = trust.Check(ctx, st.Image, "", deps)
140					verdicts[st.Image] = res
141				}
142				if f, ok := signatureFinding(rel, st, res); ok {
143					findings = append(findings, f)
144				} else if res.Verdict == trust.Failed && res.Decision == trust.Block && !reported[st.Image] {
145					// A rule asked for a guarantee that could not be checked: said
146					// once per image, as the stage's error, not as a fact.
147					reported[st.Image] = true
148					errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("%s: %s", st.Image, res.Reason()))
149				}
150			}
151		}
152		return findings, errs
153	}
154	
155	// signatureFinding is the finding a verdict makes, if it proves something.
156	func signatureFinding(file string, st dockerfile.Stage, res trust.Result) (Finding, bool) {
157		f := Finding{
158			Source: SourceSignature, IaCType: "dockerfile",
159			File: file, Line: st.Line, EndLine: st.Line,
160			Message: res.Reason(),
161			Resolution: "Pick a candidate whose signature holds in the Remediation tab. If the publisher changed its " +
162				"signing identity legitimately, update the rule in ~/.devdesk/trust.yaml.",
163		}
164		switch {
165		case res.Verdict == trust.IdentityMismatch:
166			f.ID, f.Severity = SignatureMismatchID, SeverityCritical
167			f.Title = "Base image " + st.Image + " is signed by an unexpected identity"
168			f.Description = "The image carries a valid signature, but not by the identity its rule expects. " +
169				"A tag republished with altered content and re-signed by someone else looks exactly like this, and no CVE scan would show it."
170		case res.Verdict == trust.Unsigned && res.Decision == trust.Block:
171			f.ID, f.Severity = SignatureUnsignedID, SeverityHigh
172			f.Title = "Base image " + st.Image + " is not signed as its rule requires"
173			f.Description = "A rule says images of this repository are signed, and this digest carries no signature it accepts. " +
174				"A republished tag has a new digest that none of the old signatures cover, which is what this looks like."
175		default:
176			return Finding{}, false
177		}
178		return f, true
179	}

Secret Scan: runs both scanners, and the Secrets tab shows their findings together. Misconfig Scan: detects IaC misconfigurations in Dockerfiles, Terraform, Kubernetes manifests and Helm charts (Trivy). On the Misconfigurations tab, the Source column shows the dialect each finding comes from.
K8s schema: validates a repository's Kubernetes manifests against the API schema of the configured Kubernetes version (kubeconform) — a wrong type, an unknown field, an apiVersion that release no longer serves. Its findings are on the Misconfigurations tab, with 'schema' as their source. Helm charts and Kustomize overlays are never validated raw — a template is not YAML until it is rendered. When helm is available, each chart is linted ('helm lint') and rendered, then validated; when kustomize is available, each overlay is built, then validated. A finding from a rendered resource points at its template or its kustomization, with no line. Without either tool, the results header counts them as Not rendered.
Build context: DevDesk's own check, run with the Misconfiguration category and needing no tool. A Dockerfile at the repository's root whose final image copies the whole context (COPY . or ADD .) is reported when that context holds a .git directory, or files such as .env, *.pem, *.key, id_rsa, credentials.json or .npmrc, that no .dockerignore leaves out — the git history, and a secret committed then deleted with it, would be readable from the image's layers. Only what is certain is reported: a .dockerignore pattern DevDesk cannot read, or one that may bring part of .git back, means silence. A Dockerfile below the root is not checked, since its build context is not written anywhere; the log says so. Its findings have 'context' as their source.
License Scan: analyzes dependency licenses (Trivy).
CI Score: grades a repository's pipeline configuration (plumber), for this context's forge only — a repository hosted elsewhere is not graded rather than graded without credentials. lines:
-				Body:  "For a repository, this tab reads the Dockerfiles under it and lists each base image — every stage, since a vulnerability in a build stage can reach the image that ships — with the newer tags it could move to. Candidates keep the image's variant (alpine stays alpine, slim stays slim) and its precision (3.18 is offered 3.21, not 3.21.1); by default they stay on the same major version, and the scan tab of the configuration view (Base image bumps) lets them take the next one.
Nothing is measured until you press S: each image is scanned straight from its registry, without being pulled, and the counts are kept for 24 hours. The vs now column is the change in CRITICAL plus HIGH against the image as written; negative is better. A candidate is a proposal with its evidence — the scan says the CVEs are gone, not that the application still runs on the new base.
The Update column puts an arrow on a base image whose registry has something newer: a later patch tag, or new content behind the same tag (the arrow alone — a new build) — compared with the digest the Dockerfile pins, or with the image the engine holds under that name; one the engine does not hold only gets the patch side, and shows a cloud (not local). The other states, each an icon: a check mark (up to date), an hourglass (no answer yet), a question mark in a circle (the registry did not answer), a pin (a digest with no tag, which cannot move). The registries are asked in the background when the tab opens, and each answer is kept 6 hours.
A floating tag — latest, an untagged reference, main, a codename, or a vendor tag rebuilt in place such as Docker Hardened Images' — has no version to move to, so it lists no candidates and says so. Its count is of what the tag pointed to when it was scanned, and the registry may have replaced that since: S scans it again every time, whatever its age, rather than trusting the 24 hours. Nothing is written for it — pinning it by digest would stop it following upstream fixes.
An image scan has no Dockerfile, so the tab is empty for one.
Choosing: space picks the candidate under the cursor for its stage — only one that has been scanned, since a bump is proposed with its evidence — and Enter shows what the choices would change. Ctrl+O writes them, and only when you ask: it lists each file and line, and says what git will be able to undo (a clean tracked file can be reverted with git checkout; one with uncommitted changes cannot without losing them; an untracked file or one outside a repository cannot at all). The answer defaults to No. Only the image reference changes — comments, line endings and the rest of the file are untouched — and DevDesk makes no commit, branch or push. A file that changed since the diff was computed is refused, not overwritten. A reference pinned by digest loses its pin, which the modal says. A stage that reads its image from an ARG changes that ARG's default, and a --build-arg on the command line can still override it.

content.text:
Il y a trois niveaux de test, tous depuis l'hôte, dans `.worktrees/backlog-3-90-ci-signing`. Rien de git à faire là : c'est normal que les commandes git y échouent côté hôte.

## 1. Les tests automatiques

```bash
cd .worktrees/backlog-3-90-ci-signing
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + tests
mise run test-race    # la seule vérification que le sandbox n'a pas pu faire
```

## 2. Préparer l'application

```bash
mise run build        # donne bin/dk
```

- **cosign** : rien à installer. Avec `Source: auto`, DevDesk utilise le binaire s'il est sur le PATH, sinon l'image `ghcr.io/sigstore/cosign/cosign` épinglée. Vérifie dans `:config` → onglet **tools** → groupe **Cosign** qu'il est bien détecté.
- **Les logs** sont dans `~/.devdesk/devdesk.log`. C'est là que tu verras les verdicts, les erreurs de `trust.yaml` et les commandes cosign.
- **Entre deux scénarios**, vide le cache des verdicts, qui garde un résultat 24 h (6 h pour une image non signée) :
  ```bash
  rm ~/.devdesk/cache/signature-verdicts.json
  ```

## 3. Les scénarios

### A. Sans `trust.yaml` : la liste intégrée et la continuité

Dans `:oci`, onglet Images, appuie sur `b` (navigateur de registre) et tire `G` :

| Image | Résultat attendu |
|---|---|
| `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot` | vérifiée par la règle intégrée distroless ; l'image est tirée puis taguée, pas de message |
| `cgr.dev/chainguard/static:latest` | vérifiée (règle Chainguard) |
| `busybox:1.36` | aucune politique ; tirée normalement |

Pour contrôler qu'un pull s'est fait par digest : `docker image inspect <image> --format '{{json .RepoDigests}}'`.

### B. Une règle avec la mauvaise identité : refus

Crée `~/.devdesk/trust.yaml` :

```yaml
version: 1
rules:
  - match: ghcr.io/sigstore/**
    keyless:
      issuer: https://accounts.google.com
      subject: evil@example.com
```

Ensuite, tire `ghcr.io/sigstore/cosign/cosign:v3.1.2` avec `G`.

- **Attendu** : le footer affiche en rouge « Pull of … refused: Signed by an unexpected identity — …/trust.yaml:3 ». `docker images` ne liste pas l'image. `:jobs` montre la même raison.

Remplace ensuite `evil@example.com` par `keyless@projectsigstore.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, vide le cache, et relance : le pull passe.

### C. Un `trust.yaml` invalide

Remplace `issuer:` par `isuer:`, puis relance `dk`.

- **Attendu** : au démarrage de `:oci`, le footer affiche en rouge « trust.yaml is invalid — pulls are refused… », et l'en-tête montre `Signatures: trust.yaml invalid`. Tous les pulls sont refusés, y compris busybox.

Remets le fichier en ordre après.

### D. Vérification désactivée

Dans `:config` → onglet **scan** → **Signatures** → **Image verification** : passe à `off` et sauvegarde.

- **Attendu** : l'en-tête de l'onglet Images montre `Signatures: off`, et le scénario B tire l'image sans rien vérifier. Remets `on` après.

### E. L'onglet Remediation

Prends un dépôt jetable avec ce `Dockerfile` :

```dockerfile
FROM ghcr.io/sigstore/cosign/cosign:v3.1.2 AS tool
FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot
```

Dans `:ws`, sélectionne-le, lance `S`, ouvre le résultat puis `tab` jusqu'à **Remediation**. Avec le `trust.yaml` du scénario B (mauvaise identité), tu dois obtenir :

- **Colonne `Sig`** : d'abord un sablier le temps de la vérification, puis une croix rouge sur les lignes cosign, et une coche verte sur distroless.
- **Choix bloqué** : lance `S` pour scanner les candidats, puis `space` sur un candidat cosign. Le choix est refusé, et le footer nomme la règle.
- **Scénario bis** : sans règle cosign, un candidat cosign signé par la même identité que l'image actuelle doit montrer une coche. C'est la continuité.

### F. Le finding du scan

Même dépôt, même `trust.yaml` (mauvaise identité). Relance le scan avec `ctrl+r` dans les résultats.

- **Attendu** : dans l'onglet Misconfigurations, un finding `DEVDESK-SIG-001` CRITICAL, source `signature`, ligne 1. Rien pour distroless.
- Avec `image_verification: off`, le finding disparaît.

### G. `--pull=never`

Dans `:oci`, supprime une image locale puis essaie de lancer un conteneur depuis une autre vue ou depuis une image qui n'est plus là.

- **Attendu** : le lancement échoue (« No such image »). Il ne tire jamais l'image en douce.

## Dépannage

Si un pull que tu attendais vérifié arrive avec un avertissement orange « could not be verified », regarde `devdesk.log` : cosign introuvable, ou `tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev` bloqué. Sous une règle B, un échec ne fait qu'avertir. Sous une règle C, il bloque.

Elle peut, et elle devrait probablement. J'ai mélangé deux choses :

- **Dans le fichier**, la valeur doit rester une chaîne (`on`/`off`) et pas un booléen YAML. Un fichier écrit avant que la clé existe se lirait `false`, donc « ne pas vérifier » : c'est le piège D12. Et comme seul `off` désactive, une faute de frappe laisse la vérification active.
- **Dans la vue configuration**, rien n'oblige à montrer un champ cyclique. J'ai recopié par réflexe le modèle de `base_image_track`, qui est un vrai ensemble fermé à deux valeurs nommées (`same-line`/`next-major`). La règle 132 réserve le cycle aux ensembles fermés et garde la case à cocher pour les booléens indépendants. « Vérifier ou non » est un booléen.

Le mécanisme existe déjà : une case à cocher peut lire et écrire autre chose qu'un `*bool` grâce à `get`/`set`, comme les outils cochés dans une catégorie (`scan_fields.go:119`). Pour ce champ :

```go
verify := field{Label: "Verify image signatures", Kind: kindToggle,
    get: func(c *config.Config) bool { return c.Scan.VerifiesImages() },
    set: func(c *config.Config, on bool) {
        c.Scan.ImageVerification = map[bool]string{true: config.ImageVerificationOn, false: config.ImageVerificationOff}[on]
    }}
verify.hintOn = "Signatures are checked before pulling or recommending an image — rules in ~/.devdesk/trust.yaml"
verify.hintOff = "No signature is checked; pulls go through as before"
```

Le fichier garde `on`/`off`. Une valeur tapée de travers s'affiche cochée, puisqu'elle vérifie, et le premier `space` la réécrit proprement.

Body: "For a repository, this tab reads the Dockerfiles under it and lists each base image — every stage, since a vulnerability in a build stage can reach the image that ships — with the newer tags it could move to. Candidates keep the image's variant (alpine stays alpine, slim stays slim) and its precision (3.18 is offered 3.21, not 3.21.1); by default they stay on the same major version, and the scan tab of the configuration view (Base image bumps) lets them take the next one.
Nothing is measured until you press S: each image is scanned straight from its registry, without being pulled, and the counts are kept for 24 hours. The vs now column is the change in CRITICAL plus HIGH against the image as written; negative is better. A candidate is a proposal with its evidence — the scan says the CVEs are gone, not that the application still runs on the new base.
The Update column puts an arrow on a base image whose registry has something newer: a later patch tag, or new content behind the same tag (the arrow alone — a new build) — compared with the digest the Dockerfile pins, or with the image the engine holds under that name; one the engine does not hold only gets the patch side, and shows a cloud (not local). The other states, each an icon: a check mark (up to date), an hourglass (no answer yet), a question mark in a circle (the registry did not answer), a pin (a digest with no tag, which cannot move). The registries are asked in the background when the tab opens, and each answer is kept 6 hours.
A floating tag — latest, an untagged reference, main, a codename, or a vendor tag rebuilt in place such as Docker Hardened Images' — has no version to move to, so it lists no candidates and says so. Its count is of what the tag pointed to when it was scanned, and the registry may have replaced that since: S scans it again every time, whatever its age, rather than trusting the 24 hours. Nothing is written for it — pinning it by digest would stop it following upstream fixes.
An image scan has no Dockerfile, so the tab is empty for one.
Choosing: space picks the candidate under the cursor for its stage — only one that has been scanned, since a bump is proposed with its evidence — and Enter shows what the choices would change. Ctrl+O writes them, and only when you ask: it lists each file and line, and says what git will be able to undo (a clean tracked file can be reverted with git checkout; one with uncommitted changes cannot without losing them; an untracked file or one outside a repository cannot at all). The answer defaults to No. Only the image reference changes — comments, line endings and the rest of the file are untouched — and DevDesk makes no commit, branch or push. A file that changed since the diff was computed is refused, not overwritten. A reference pinned by digest loses its pin, which the modal says. C'est commité : `401fe367`. Lint : 0 problème, et `go test ./...` passe.

- **`:config` → onglet scan → Signatures** : le réglage est maintenant une case à cocher, **Verify image signatures**, qu'on bascule avec `space`. L'aide sous la case change selon qu'elle est cochée ou non.
- **Le fichier ne change pas** : il garde `on`/`off`. Un fichier sans la clé s'affiche coché. Une valeur mal tapée aussi, puisqu'elle vérifie, et le premier `space` la réécrit proprement.
- **Un test couvre ces quatre cas** : fichier sans la clé, décocher, recocher, valeur mal tapée.
- **Autour** : les aides des vues OCI et sécurité pointent vers le nouveau libellé. J'ai supprimé `ImageVerifications()`, que seul le champ cyclique utilisait, et ajouté l'écart n° 11 à §3.82.

Pour ton scénario D du guide de test, il suffit donc de décocher **Verify image signatures** au lieu de passer à `off`.
